title: Interpretable Latents in a Neutrino Foundation Model with Sparse Autoencoders
hook: Sparse autoencoders find physics concepts in an IceCube foundation model — and show its direction head barely uses them. A head that does cuts angular error from 20.2 to 3.2 degrees.
key_points: First application of SAE-based mechanistic interpretability to particle physics.
The subject is a neutrino foundation model pretrained on IceCube data, fine-tuned for direction reconstruction.
A validated atlas of physical concepts was extracted from the model's representation.
Causal interventions show the direction head barely draws on this atlas — the information is learned but underused.
An uncertainty head trained on the same representation depends causally on the atlas's quality and brightness features.
At 20% selection efficiency it improves median angular resolution from 20.2 to 3.2 degrees.
content_html: Sparse autoencoders have become the standard tool for pulling interpretable features out of language models. Bonnet-Guerrini and colleagues apply them somewhere new: a neutrino foundation model pretrained on IceCube detector data and fine-tuned for direction reconstruction. It's the first SAE-based mechanistic interpretability work in particle physics.
extra_html:
A validated atlas

The authors identify an atlas of physical concepts encoded in the model's representation, held to a strict validation protocol — held-out tests, matched nuisance controls, and replication across independent dictionary trainings. That bar matters here, because SAE features are notoriously easy to over-interpret. Then causal interventions deliver the surprise: the direction head barely draws on this atlas. The model has learned physics it isn't using for its own task.

Interpretability that pays

Rather than stopping at the diagnosis, the authors act on it. They train an uncertainty head on the same event-level representation to predict the model's angular reconstruction error. Unlike the direction head, this one depends causally on quality and brightness features from the atlas — it's consuming exactly the information that was going to waste. At 20% selection efficiency, the resulting interpretable estimator improves median angular resolution from 20.2 degrees to 3.2 degrees. That's the argument in miniature: mechanistic interpretability can reveal latent physics inside a model's representation and then guide the design of downstream tasks that exploit it. arXiv, 2026.

related.hook: Clamping a 'harmful' sparse-autoencoder feature looks like it stops bad behavior — but this paper recovers it 95.8% of the time, exposing the gap between feature-level and real control.

choices.text: They trained an uncertainty head on the same representation to predict angular reconstruction error, exploiting the underused features
They retrained the direction head from scratch with more data
They pruned the unused features to shrink the model

flashcards.explanation_html: The new head depends causally on the atlas's quality and brightness features, and at 20% selection efficiency improves median angular resolution from 20.2 to 3.2 degrees.

flashcards.prompt: What validation protocol did the concept atlas have to pass?
flashcards.back_html: Held-out tests, matched nuisance controls, and replication across independently trained dictionaries — a strict bar, since SAE features are easy to over-interpret.
